analysis.title: GS MORNING: 1) FX Trader Call Today, 2) FOMC Preview, 3) 2 Mins Read on Fed, ECB, BOJ, 4) RBNZ Recap and 5) USDCNH Trade Idea 28 Oct 2026
key_insights: GS expects the FOMC to skip a hike at the October meeting and deliver a second hike in December, based on FOMC comments pointing to a compromise of raising rates every other meeting.

Financial conditions have tightened moderately since September after the Fed's hawkish pivot. GS says this is only a bit more than usually accompanies one hike and much less than the four hikes the market has priced, so the FOMC is unlikely to treat it as a substitute for hikes.

The key October FOMC communication question is how the statement sentence on the September hike changes. GS thinks it may adapt Vice Chair Jefferson's language: further adjustments 'will depend on trends in the data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks.' GS expects no significant new information from the press conference.

If the FOMC keeps an every-other-meeting pace in 2027, a March 2027 hike is possible. GS does not expect one because it expects inflation to improve as tariff, energy shock and AI price pressures fade. Growth or employment concerns would also end the hikes.

Fed surprise risk: Warsh echoing Waller that hikes need not come at consecutive meetings and stressing 'no pre-set pace' likely keeps the hike premium priced into 2027. The clearest misstep risk is a repeat of July, when Warsh's most dovish answers came while explaining why the Fed was not hiking, so the market could read the press conference as dovish.

On Fed rates: more airtime on inflation likely extends curve flattening and keeps the front end selling off. More discussion of tighter financial conditions likely re-steepens the curve. With about 75bps priced through Q3 2027, GS sees a 15bp rally as more likely than a selloff. In FX, AUDUSD likely moves most on a hawkish Fed surprise.

ECB: the statement is not expected to mention sovereign spreads. Lagarde will likely call France a political problem rather than a monetary one and say the ECB has tools to contain contagion. A dismissive or very hawkish tone on French spreads is the bigger risk for EUR fixed income. Fewer hikes would be bearish for EUR and bullish for Bunds. Credit easing or transmission tools would be bullish for EUR and the periphery.

BOJ: base case is a mildly dovish pause with underlying inflation converging toward 2%. Board members will likely cut the FY26 core inflation forecast and raise FY27 on energy. GS expects a gradual post-meeting rates sell-off, with the medium-term terminal rate expectation of 2.00%+ intact. The BOJ will not push back on a December hike (about 80% priced), mindful of USDJPY rising back above 160.

RBNZ held the OCR at 2.75% on a 4-3 split vote. Markets had priced 24.4bp of tightening and 23 of 25 Bloomberg-surveyed economists, including GS, expected a hike. Governor Breman voted to hold but said nine times in the press conference that further OCR increases are likely, and that tightening may be a bit more than said in September, when the 2027 peak was projected at 3.15%.
GS now forecasts RBNZ hikes of 25bp in December to 3.00% and 25bp in March to 3.25%, the mid-point of GS and RBNZ neutral estimates. This is below market pricing of 3.75% by August 2027.

AUDNZD rose through 1.26 after the dovish RBNZ hold, a 1.6% low-to-high move that outperformed the roughly 50bp implied gap by more than 3x. Dealers trade short gamma in AUDNZD, and clients showed fresh NZDUSD downside demand to own NZD downside over the election.

GS EM FX options trade idea: buy 3-month USDCNH 6.575 digital puts at 19.70% USD offer, about 5x max leverage, forward reference 6.6190, max loss limited to premium paid. The thesis is that CNH has been resilient, with USDCNH grinding lower while DXY stayed firm in the first half of October and risk sentiment fell on an AI/tech equity sell-off.

GS argues USDCNH vol is in the bottom 10th percentile, driven by corporate structured supply. 1-month implied vol of 1.3 implies a 195pip straddle breakeven, yet USDCNH spot moved about 475pip lower over the past month and the fixing about 234pip lower. The digi price implies under 20% probability of a roughly 300pip per month move lower over three months, which GS sees as conservative.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS says the market-implied path is well ahead of what the recent tightening in financial conditions would justify, and GS expects an every-other-meeting pace.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish: the market prices four hikes and about 75bps through Q3 2027, and Warsh's 'no pre-set pace' message could keep the hike premium in 2027. More airtime on inflation would extend curve flattening and keep the front end selling off.
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish: GS expects an every-other-meeting pace with a skip in October, and tighter financial conditions could re-steepen the curve. A repeat of July could make the press conference read dovish. GS sees a 15bp rally as more likely than a selloff.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Growth or employment concerns would end the hikes, and an improving inflation trend would argue against a March 2027 hike.
